claim: EARWIG is the move-and-start earwig routine this module ports.
EARWIG runs only while the player is alive — the PLAYP EOR 0A / PEXPLD gate at entry returns when either is set.
The earwig lives in motion-object slot 12 (decimal) — BEEC+12 is probed for occupancy at entry.
With slot 12 occupied, a picture at or above 0x1E is not an earwig and the routine returns.
A slot-12 picture at or above 0x1C (and below 0x1E) IS the earwig, and the routine jumps to its move path — the pics band is [1C,1E).

source.verbatim: BCS 50$			;THIS IS A EARWIG MOVE HIM

claim: The earwig may only start on the tick where the FULL frame byte is zero — once every 256 frames ("EVERY 4 SECONDS").
CENTIN is compared against decimal 11 for the start gate.
CENTIN at or above 11 blocks the start — the earwig waits for waves where the centipede is small.

source.verbatim: BCS 2$			;WAIT UNTIL WAVES WHERE THE CENTIPEDE IS SMALL

claim: The start is further gated on RND0 AND 3 being zero — a 1-in-4 random entry.
The earwig spawn picture is 0x1C.
The earwig spawn colour is 0xB9.
Below a SCORE2 of 2 (20,000) the earwig always uses the slow speed.
From 20,000 a fresh RND0 read AND 3 equal to zero still randomly picks the slow earwig.
The fast earwig speed is 2.
The horizontal direction is chosen by a fresh RND0 read — BIT RND0, bit 7 clear keeps the positive speed.
Bit 7 set makes the fast speed negative — dh -2 (0xFE).
The slow earwig speed is 1.
Bit 7 set makes the slow speed negative — dh -1 (0xFF).
The chosen signed speed is stored to BEEDH+12.
The earwig starts at H = 0 — the screen edge.
The vertical direction BEEDV+12 is cleared to 0 — the earwig never dives.
The spawn V is built from a fresh RND0 read masked with 0x78.
The masked byte gets 0x70 added — the V range is 0x70..0xE8.
The sum (EOR CKF8, identity upright) is stored as BEEV+12 — the upper half of the screen.

source.verbatim: STA BEEV+12.		;SET VERTICAL POSITION IN UPPER HALF OF SCREEN

claim: Each move tick adds BEEDH+12 to BEEH+12 — pure horizontal motion.
A new H of exactly zero means the earwig walked off screen.
The off-screen exit jumps to BEEOFF — the slot is reset to allow bees.

source.verbatim: JMP BEEOFF		;RESET ENTRY TO ALLOW BEES

claim: The picture flaps only on frames where FRAME AND 3 is zero — every fourth frame.
The flap toggles the picture with EOR 1.
The playfield stamp under the earwig comes from OBSTAC at Y=0 with A=BEEV+12 — a caller-side seam.
A stamp below CLOUD is not a DDT explosion.
A stamp at or above DDT is not a DDT explosion — the death band is [CLOUD, DDT).
A stamp inside the DDT band kills the earwig via DDTEX1 — the death-sequence seam.
A stamp below 0x7C is not a mushroom and is left alone.
A mushroom stamp is poisoned by clearing bit 2 — AND 0xFB.
The poisoned stamp is written back to the playfield.
CLOUD is 0x2E — the first DDT explosion-cloud stamp.
DDT is 0x6E — the first of the two DDT bomb stamps.

source.verbatim: DDT	=6E			;FIRST OF 2 STAMPS FOR DDT BOMB

claim: SHOOT2 classifies a masked picture below 0x1E (and at or above 0x1C) as an earwig.
An earwig kill scores 1000 — LDY I,10 is the BCD hundreds byte.
An earwig killed by DDT scores 3000 — BCD 30 hundreds.
The band below 0x1C belongs to the spider — the earwig lower bound.
WRMMV is the enter-and-move inchworm routine this module ports.
WRMMV runs only while the player is alive — the PLAYP EOR 0A / PEXPLD gate at entry.
The inchworm uses motion-object slot 0 — bare MOBJC, no index.
A non-zero MOBJC means the entry is in use and the routine goes to the move path.
The inchworm may only enter on the tick where the frame low byte equals 0x13.
The frame HIGH byte AND 3 must also be zero — one spawn window every 4 wraps ("EVERY 16 RECORDS").
CENTIN is compared against decimal 11 — at or above blocks the entry as too soon.
DEAD equal to zero blocks the entry — the inchworm does NOT enter while the centipede is dead.

source.verbatim: BEQ 1$			;DO NOT ENTER IF CENTIPEDE IS DEAD

claim: A picture at or above 0x14 is not an inchworm.
A picture below 0x10 is not an inchworm — the pics band is [10,14).
The next picture is pic + 1 — the ADC I,0 rides the carry the band check left SET.
The incremented picture is masked with 0x13, wrapping the cycle 10→11→12→13→10.
MOBJDH is one of -2, -1, 1 or 2.
The flap mask starts from |MOBJDH| ORA 1 — 1 if slow, 3 if fast.

source.verbatim: ORA I,01		;1 IF SLOW, 3 IF FAST

claim: EOR 2 inverts it — mask 3 if slow, 1 if fast: the slow worm animates every 4 frames, the fast one every 2.

source.verbatim: EOR I,02		;3 IF SLOW, 1 IF FAST

claim: The mask is ANDed with FRAME — the picture only updates when the result is zero.
On an update tick the cycled picture is stored back to MOBJP.
Each move tick adds MOBJDH to MOBJH — pure horizontal motion.
A new H of exactly zero means the inchworm walked off screen.
Off screen, only MOBJC is cleared — removed from the active list (no BEEOFF: PTS is left alone).

source.verbatim: STA MOBJC		;REMOVE FROM THE ACTIVE LIST

claim: The move tail runs OBSTAC then jumps to DDTEXP — caller-side explosion seams.
The inchworm spawn picture is 0x10.
The inchworm spawn colour is 0xB9.
The inchworm starts at H = 0.
The spawn V is built from RND1 masked with 0x38.
The masked byte gets 0x40 added — the V range is 0x40..0x78.
The sum is stored as MOBJV.
The base speed byte is 2.
SCORE2 at or above 8 (80,000) keeps the fast speed 2.
Below 80,000 the speed is 1.
The direction is chosen by RND0 bit 7 — set runs COMP and goes the opposite way.
The signed speed is stored to MOBJDH.
SHOOT2 classifies a masked picture below 0x14 (and at or above 0x10) as an inchworm.
An inchworm kill FIRST sets SLOW to 0xE0 — slowing down all critters — before any scoring.
An inchworm kill scores 100 — BCD 1 hundreds.

source.verbatim: LDY I,1			;100 POINTS FOR AN INCHWORM

claim: An inchworm killed by DDT scores 300 — BCD 3 hundreds.
The SLOW byte loaded for the inchworm kill is 0xE0.
BEEMV is the move-bee-down-screen routine this module ports.
BEEMV runs only while the player is alive — the PLAYP EOR 0A / PEXPLD gate at entry.
The bee spawn slot is motion object 12 (decimal) — BEEC+12 is probed for availability.
A non-zero BEEC+12 means the entry is taken and no bee starts this tick.
While the centipede is NOT dead (DEAD non-zero) the spawn goes through the mushroom-count check.
With the centipede dead and NO beetles on screen, the spawn also goes through the mushroom-count check.
With the centipede dead and a beetle on screen, CENTIN at or above decimal 10 spawns the bee DIRECTLY, skipping the mushroom check.
BEEMV1 supplies the count of mushrooms needed for the spawn decision.

source.verbatim: 3$:	JSR BEEMV1		;GET COUNT OF MUSHROOMS NEEDED

claim: A needed-count below MUSH (mushrooms near the bottom) blocks the spawn — the bee enters only when few mushrooms remain.

source.verbatim: BCC 5$			;IF THERE ARE MANY MUSHROOMS NEAR BOTTOM

claim: The spawn path loads X with 12 and calls BEEMV3.
The movement sweep scans motion slots from 12 DOWN to 0 — any slot can carry a bee picture.
A picture at or above 0x3A is not a bee.
A picture below 0x38 is not a bee — the pics band is [38,3A).
The wings flap only on EVEN frames — FRAME AND 1 non-zero skips the picture change.
The flap toggles the picture with EOR 1.
Each live bee moves through the shared BEEMV0 helper.

source.verbatim: JSR BEEMV0		;MOVE BEE AND CHECK COLLISIONS

claim: BEEMV0 SUBTRACTS BEEDV from BEEV — the dive.
A post-move V below 4 is the bottom of the screen and the slot goes to BEEOFF.
The mushroom cell is 4 above the slot V — "MAKE MUSHROOM APPEAR AFTER BEE".

source.verbatim: LDA I,4			;MAKE MUSHROOM APPEAR AFTER BEE

claim: Attract mode SKIPS the bombing-mode veto and always reaches the plant roll.
A non-zero NOCENT ("bomb" mode) vetoes mushroom planting outside attract.
Mushrooms are only planted on frames where FRAME AND 3 is zero — every fourth frame.

source.verbatim: BNE 28$			;PUT UP MUSHROOMS ONLY EVERY FOUR FRAMES

claim: A slot picture at or above 0x20 takes the BEE plant mask.
The bee plant mask is 3 — a 1-in-4 roll, everywhere on screen.
The mask is ANDed with RND1 — non-zero means no mushroom.
BEEOFF clears the slot PTS byte.
BEEOFF clears the colour — the slot is freed.
BEEOFF clears H too, preventing blanking other motion objects.

source.verbatim: STA X,BEEH		;PREVENTS BLANKING OTHER MOTION OBJECTS

claim: BEEMV1: below a SCORE2 of 2 (20,000) the needed count is 5.
BEEMV1: from 20,000 the needed count is 9.
BEEMV1: below 120,000 (SCORE2 0x12) the 5/9 value stands.
BEEMV1: from 120,000 the needed count is the halved SCORE2 byte plus 6.

source.verbatim: ADC I,6			;INCREASE MINIMUM NUMBER OF MUSHROOMS

claim: BEEMV1: the needed count is capped at 0x2F.
BEEMV3: SCORE2 at or above 6 (60,000) makes the bee faster.
BEEMV3: the fast bee dive speed is 3.
BEEMV3: the normal bee dive speed is 2.
The bee spawn picture is 0x38.
BEEMV2: the spawn V byte is 0xF8 (EOR CKF8, identity upright) — the top row.
BEEMV2: the spawn column masks RND0 with 0xF8.
BEEMV2: a masked byte below 0x10 is off screen and rerolls.
BEEMV2: the accepted byte has 4 subtracted for the H position.
BEEMV2: BEEDH is cleared to 0 — the bee flies straight down.
BEEMV2: the on-colour is 0x79.
SHOOT2 classifies a masked picture at or above 0x38 as a bee.
A bee kill scores 200 — BCD 2 hundreds.

source.verbatim: 127$:	LDY I,2			;200 POINTS FOR AN BEE

claim: A bee killed by DDT scores 600 — BCD 6 hundreds.
The hit byte is 4 (EOR CKF8, identity upright) — compared against the slot BEEDV.
A BEEDV already equal to 4 means the SECOND hit — time to explode the bee, and scoring proceeds.
On the FIRST hit the 4 is STORED to BEEDV — the bee speeds up instead of dying.

source.verbatim: STA X,BEEDV		;SPEED UP ON FIRST HIT

claim: The first hit exits with carry clear — NO scoring yet.
PTS is the 16-entry kill-points stamp array BEEOFF clears into.

source.verbatim: PTS:	.BLKB 16.		;NUMBER OF POINTS FOR KILLING THIS CRITTER
